judged_by: Matched by a Claude Opus 5.5 agent on 2026-11-22; not yet checked by the labeler.

question.note: Phrased as what the paper argues, but its subject is the spillover of the 'convicted criminal' advertisement onto perceptions of people with records (Q1); same call as the calibration note's question entry [0].

central_claim.note: Gives the ad's harm to perceptions and its improvement of feelings of representation; omits the counter-narrative's offset.

evidence.note: E2: total N and the three arms (counts in the quote). E1 partial: survey experiment with U.S. Democrats, without pre-registration, Prolific or dates.
Counter-narrative half of E3 (formerly incarcerated legislator Jovan Jackson; the quote names the news article). The ad stimulus is not described.
Five-item perceptions index with alpha 0.71: one part of E4. Reliability reported without calling it a limitation, so no L7.
The counter-narrative's increase relative to the ad alone is F2, a finding in the evidence slot. Keeps the comparison, so no flag.

F4 (reduced ad support) and F5 (reduced perceived quality of Democratic representation, vs the ad alone per the quotes). The first quote is in the paper, so the entry is grounded; the F5 quote is not in the paper.

flags.text: 'The counter-narrative significantly increases positive perceptions' drops that it was shown before the ad and is compared with the ad alone; there was no counter-narrative-only arm (p.16). The quote keeps the qualification.

key_findings.note: H1C (value of representation, 0.79 SD vs ad alone) is accurate to p.11 but not a gold answer; only quote NOT IN PAPER.

scope_and_limits.note: Gives the gap to behavior with self-reports and 'long-term'; the quote lists durability and repeated exposure but the claim states only the behavior part. Same call as the calibration note's behavior-only entry.
'Does not fully disentangle' is a little softer than 'not possible' (p.17); substance kept.

flags.text: Says the paper extends social categorization theory by incorporating perspective-getting. The paper grounds the counter-narrative in separate perspective-getting and counter-stereotype research (p.3, p.15); it does not present it as an extension of social categorization theory.

theoretical_positioning.note: Partial T2 for perspective-getting as the counter-narrative mechanism; same call as the calibration note's entry that tied the counter-narrative to social categorization theory.

flags.text: Says the paper disputes a claim that stigmatizing messaging increases support for punitive policies. The cited finding (p.2, [11]) is that anger toward people with records is associated with support for punitive policy, and the paper uses it as support for its concern, not something it disputes.
Says such messaging 'reduces feelings of representation'. The paper finds the ad improved perceived representation (p.1, p.11, p.15).
